intervals.label: Tibet air-shower arrays (Tibet-I, -II, -III)
intervals.note: Start of the first (Tibet-I) array at Yangbajing. The 2002 text says that array ran three years before many scintillation counters were added (Tibet-II). The ICRR chronology dates the construction of the "air shower gamma ray detector in Tibet" to 1993 and its completion to 1997 (Heisei 5 and 9). No source read reconciles the two.

intervals.label: Tibet-III array
intervals.quote: The Tibet-III air shower array, consisting of 533 scintillation detectors, has been operating successfully at Yangbajing in Tibet, China since 1999.

intervals.label: air-shower array with underground muon detectors
intervals.note: The underground water-Cherenkov muon-detector (MD) array, about 3,400 m2, beneath the air-shower array; a 100 m2 prototype was built in 2007. Allows hadron rejection above 100 TeV.

name: Tibet air-shower array and underground muon-detector array

placements.quote: In collaboration with China, an air shower observation array is built at Yangbajing (4300m above sea level, 90.53 deg E,30.11 deg N) in Tibet, China to observe high-energy cosmic rays.

altitude.quote: Yangbajing (4300m above sea level, 90.53 deg E,30.11 deg N)

area.quote: The current AS array, covering an area of 65,700 m2

summary.plain: Scintillator panels over about 65,000 square metres of the Tibetan plateau, with underground water tanks that tell gamma-ray showers from cosmic-ray showers.
summary.technical: Tibet AS array (597 scintillation detectors of 0.5 m2 in 2019, 65,700 m2) plus underground water-Cherenkov muon-detector array (3,400 m2, since 2014); angular resolution about 1 degree measured with the Moon's shadow.

technology.quote: Each counter has a plate of plastic scintillator, 0.5 m2 in area and 3 cm in thickness, equipped with a 2-inch-in-diameter photomultiplier tube (PMT).
technology.value: Array of plastic-scintillator detectors measuring air-shower arrival time and density, with an underground water-Cherenkov muon-detector array for gamma/hadron discrimination.
